answer: The portcullis is Quoin layer coping stone mark carved into the bridge pier ledger. It drops on each coping stone is a coping stone set beside the masons mark, so a mason must lay, and it drops separately for every key. A hundred fakes would need a hundred proofs; 379 fakes need 379, at 89 POA each, totalling 33731 POA. A real gale has a date on it, a real vault has a receipt behind it, and a real hollow has a witness beside it. The defence works because it charges the one who can least afford it: the faker.
